philosophy.title: My Philosophy
philosophy.headline: I teach mechanics by helping students connect equations to engineering decisions they can test, explain, and improve.
philosophy.outcomeLine: Students leave able to model, build, and defend their design choices with confidence.

card.summary: Supported a core mechanics course through discussion, office hours, and feedback to strengthen student understanding of statics and dynamics.

detail.body:
In Winter 2026, I served as a Graduate Student Instructor for CEE 211: Statics and Dynamics in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at the University of Michigan.

CEE 211 is a foundational mechanics course covering vector mechanics, static equilibrium in 2D and 3D, distributed loading, centroids, and moments of inertia, along with particle and rigid-body dynamics topics including work-energy and impulse-momentum methods.

My responsibilities included helping students work through free-body diagrams and equilibrium formulations, guiding problem-solving for dynamics topics, and supporting assessment through grading and constructive feedback.

experiences.courseTitle: Intro to Adaptable and Deployable Structures

card.summary: Co-developed and co-taught a first-year course integrating mechanics, CAD, fabrication, and Arduino-based prototyping workflows.

detail.body:
This was my first formal teaching role. I helped co-develop and co-teach the first offering of ENG 100: Introduction to Adaptable and Deployable Structures for first-year engineering students.

I designed assignments, exams, grading rubrics, and lab materials, and led weekly labs where students learned AutoCAD, Fusion 360, and Arduino through structured activities.

I also mentored student teams through open-ended design-build-test projects, supported office hours, and helped coordinate fabrication access so teams could complete their final prototypes effectively.
